title: Fix Unity-NUnit compile blocker: Is.AnyOf in ReaccionaMicrogameTests (headless NUnit 3.14 vs Unity's bundled NUnit divergence)
description: Found during the Hito-4 Unity compile gate (2026-07-08). The Unity EditMode test assembly FAILS TO COMPILE due to a single pre-existing error: ReaccionaMicrogameTests.cs:596 `Assert.That(r.Seat, Is.AnyOf((int)PlayerSlot.Rojo, (int)PlayerSlot.Azul));`. `Is.AnyOf` was added in NUnit 3.6; the headless fast-tests project references NUnit 3.14.0 (so the headless suite compiles+passes), but Unity's Test Framework bundles an OLDER NUnit that lacks `Is.AnyOf` → CS0117 'Is' does not contain a definition for 'AnyOf', which blocks the ENTIRE Unity EditMode assembly (one error fails all EditMode tests in Unity). Pre-existing (Reacciona/TASK-051-052 era), not from the Hito-4 run — the new Board/ and Bots/ Core code compiles clean in Unity. IMMEDIATE FIX: replace the one line with a construct valid in BOTH NUnit versions, e.g. `Assert.That(r.Seat, Is.EqualTo((int)PlayerSlot.Rojo).Or.EqualTo((int)PlayerSlot.Azul));` (semantically identical). Must keep the headless fast suite green AND make the Unity EditMode assembly compile. BROADER NOTE (for a possible separate follow-up): the headless csproj (NUnit 3.14) and Unity's bundled NUnit can diverge silently — the headless gate won't catch Unity-incompatible NUnit constructs. Consider aligning the headless NUnit version to Unity's, or adding a periodic Unity-compile check, so this class of divergence is caught by the primary gate. Grep confirmed Is.AnyOf is the ONLY occurrence in Assets today.
acceptance_criteria: ReaccionaMicrogameTests.cs:596 no longer uses Is.AnyOf; replaced with an equivalent (Is.EqualTo(a).Or.EqualTo(b) or similar) valid in both NUnit 3.14 (headless) and Unity's bundled NUnit
The headless fast suite stays green (the test still passes, same assertion semantics)
The Unity EditMode test assembly compiles clean (verified via MCP recompile / get_console_logs: zero errors)
Grep confirms no other Is.AnyOf (or other known-divergent newer-NUnit constructs) remain unaddressed in Assets
